The link on ``no ontologically basic mental things'' goes to ``Excluding the Supernatural'' (12 September 2008), which the book prints later.}

\cpara{Cites the gratitude list as ``an old trick.'' It has some support. In experiments by Emmons and McCullough (2003), people assigned to list things they were grateful for showed ``heightened well-being across several, though not all, of the outcome measures.''}

\cpara{The post's proposal, a variant of the gratitude list: list abilities that would seem amazing if they were magic, or if only a few people had them. The second link goes to ``Joy in Discovery.''}
\cpara{The first example: binocular vision described as a magic second eye.}
\cpara{Proposes that the ability would be appreciated only under an impressive name, ``Mystic Eyes of Depth Perception.''}
\cpara{Writing and copying, which let the dead share their thoughts with the living. The last clause warns, it seems, against using ideas one could not have worked out oneself.}
\cpara{Hands, and tool-making, described as a feedback loop in which tools make finer tools.}

\cpara{Sight, described as sensing ``tiny vibrations'' in ``the Force that binds matter,'' that is, light as an electromagnetic wave. The last line echoes the proverb that in the land of the blind the one-eyed man is king.}

\cpara{The last and longest item is intelligence: an inner model of the world used to steer toward chosen futures. It restates, in the language of fantasy, ``The Power of Intelligence'' (1 January 2007), which spoke of ``the power to search paths through the great web of causality.''}
\cpara{Claims that intelligence overcomes every lesser power and extends its understanding across galaxies and aeons, down to the ``world beneath the world'' of physics.}
\cpara{Grants that intelligent beings die in catastrophes and surprise attacks, and calls such victories luck.}
\cpara{Adds that intelligence can destroy its bearer through flaws in its model of the world.}
\cpara{Says intelligence, unlike weapons or limbs, cannot be taken away: it is ``the power that cannot be removed without removing you.''}

\cpara{Turns to moral status: the Ultimates hold that their power is part of what makes a creature ``an end in itself,'' and that those without it cannot understand why. The post calls this ``a suspiciously self-serving argument.''}

\cfact{``Schiavo'' is Italian for ``slave,'' not a word for ``dead while breathing.'' It appears to refer to Terri Schiavo, a woman in a permanent vegetative state whose care was fought over in American courts and legislatures from 1998 to 2005; two commenters on the post singled the word out as a joke.}
\cpara{Ends the list, and the post: the bearers of intelligence rule all other life. The post does not return to its opening proposal.}
